items.title: SP-API Release Notes
items.excerpt: Selling Partner API new features, software updates, and changelog.
items.body: For releases prior to January 19, 2022, refer to Announcements in the Selling Partner API GitHub repo . July 29, 2026 API changes Invoices API v2026-06-25 Launched the new Invoices API. You can use the Invoices API to retrieve invoice data programmatically and streamline your bookkeeping processes. The Invoices API enables you to search for invoices within a specified date range, track invoice payment status, and retrieve detailed line-item information for reconciliation with purchase orders. For more information, refer to Invoices API . Finances v2024-06-19 Added the listSummary operation that enables you to retrieve a financial summary for a date range or settlement Added the listBalances operation that enables you to retrieve a current or past balance. Added the SETTLEMENT_ID value for the relatedIdentifierName query parameter for the listTransactions operation. You can use this value to filter transactions by their settlement ID. Fulfillment Inbound v2024-03-20 Added an optional discounts field to the listDeliveryWindowOptions response with discount incentives for delivery window options. This enables you to view available discounts as you select delivery windows that have the DISCOUNTED availability type. Fulfillment Outbound v2026-07-04 Launched a new version of the Fulfillment Outbound API. This new version supports granular dynamic sandbox controls, multi-tenant authorization, async processing support, among other improvements. Refer to Fulfillment Outbound Migration Guide for more information. Listings Items API v2021-08-01 Updated the marketplaceIds parameter in the getListingsItem and searchListingsItems operations to accept multiple marketplaceIds within the same region. You can use these operations to retrieve listings data across multiple stores in a sing...

Ivan shares how he went from working at Microsoft to acquiring an established seven-figure e-commerce business—and eventually tripling its revenue. While Amazon remains Ivan’s largest channel, his company has built a much broader operation through its own websites, independent retailers, regional distributors, Walmart, eBay, TikTok Shop, and Faire. Ivan explains how wholesale volume, strong supplier relationships, and European manufacturing allow Meltonian to maintain healthy margins on products selling for as little as $7.99. He also breaks down why managing inventory in-house makes sense for a business carrying thousands of SKUs across multiple sales channels. Ivan also reveals how his team uses Helium 10 tools such as Cerebro and Magnet to rank for valuable non-branded keywords and develop new products based on customer demand, competitor gaps, and search behavior.
